summary: This is a Makefile target that creates a quick checkpoint of work-in-progress code. When you run 'make git_wip', it stages all changes, commits them with a 'wip' message while skipping pre-commit hooks, and pushes to the remote repository — useful for saving your work without worrying about code quality checks.

explanations.1: In Makefiles, a target name followed by a colon defines a recipe that can be run by typing 'make' followed by that name.
explanations.3: The --no-verify flag tells git to skip any pre-commit hooks (automated checks that might otherwise block the commit), which is common when you just want to save rough work quickly.
